To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the studied mountain populations of Scots pine ( Pinus sylvestr is L.) from the Polish mountains and foothills show a higher degree of differentiation than lowland populations.

the studied populations differ significantly in the studied needle traits, the division of the studied population into two groups (one mountainous and one lowland) is reflected in the results, and a particularly strong relationship is found between two relicts from the Pienińskie Mts. (Sokolica and Kazalnica) and Tatra Mt. (Wielkie Koryciska).
the needle traits of studied Scots pine populations from mountain and foothill areas are different from those of lowland populations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the variability of morphological traits of the needles in the Scots pine, which is one of the most important tree species in Europe and the most common in Poland.
the variability of morphological needle characters among natural populations of Scots pine from the mountainous and lowland regions in Poland.
the variability of needle traits of Scots pines from mountainous, foothill and lowland regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the needle traits of the studied populations are a good indicator of their origin.

the studied mountain populations of Scots pine are characterized by a high level of variability in the needle traits, which is reflected in a large number of statistically significant differences in comparison with the lowland populations.
mountainous populations are characterized by higher needle length, higher number of stomata on the convex side and lower number of serrations on the left and right side.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the needle traits of Scots pines from the Tatra Mountains and from the Pienin Mountains are more similar to each other than to the needles of Scots pines of other populations.

the examined populations differ in their morphological needle characteristics, which may be related to the environmental factors, and the postulated division into two groups is also reflected in the obtained data.
the needle traits variability of studied populations is the result of the interaction of genetic and environmental factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the studied populations of Scots pine are characterized by a high degree of differentiation and the existence of two groups of populations.
the studied populations of Scots pine from Poland can be divided into two groups: mountain and lowland.
the needle traits of Scots pines from the Tatra Mts., which are considered to be the most valuable, are not significantly different from the ones of the lowland populations.
